List of Best Law Courses in Canada after 12th for Indian Students: Colleges, Eligibility & Ranking

Students who want to study abroad in Canada can go through our list of best law courses in Canada after 12th for Indian students. One Window provides the information about overseas education in Canada, India student visa process and ranking of various colleges from across Canada which offer excellent courses like Bachelor of Laws (LLB), Bachelor of Commerce (BCom), Bachelors in Business Administration (BBA), etc. For more details, Read.

Explore Top Colleges

To study abroad on a student visa to Canada or to find higher education courses at overseas universities and colleges that accept international students who want to pursue law studies , consider doing a bit of research about various Canadian educational institutions offering law courses. To help you with your search, we’ve curated a list of some good colleges and universities offering law courses both at bachelors and post-graduate levels. For more details about these top law schools, read on.

Course Details

A foreign student requires a study permit if they want to study at a university, college or other type of school in Canada. However, they are not required to hold a valid study permit while they’re studying at a designated learning institution (DLI). International students planning on doing any kind of coursework or training that takes more than six months will require an open work permit. You cannot apply for a work permit through your Study Permit; you have to apply separately by creating an account on Global Affairs Canada’s website.

    Top-Ranked University In Toronto (Canada)

    The University of Toronto is Canada’s top-ranked university, placed ninth overall on a list of 75 Best Global Universities by U.S. News and World Report. According to Forbes Magazine (2018), it is also North America’s third best value for international students.

      Eligibility for admission in university of Toronto

      Undergraduate applicants should have a minimum C+ (73% if using a 4-point scale) average or equivalent as determined by their high school and faculty. For example: A 73% average is required to be eligible for most Arts and Science courses. A 79% average is required to be eligible for most Engineering courses. You are also encouraged to see How do I calculate my overall average? here on our website.

      [content_block id=14313 slug=zoho-form]

        The University Of Calgary (Canada)

        The University of Calgary is a public research university located in Calgary, Alberta. Founded by royal charter on September 1, 1966, and originally operated out of two buildings on land leased from the City of Calgary before moving to its current location.

          Eligibility for admission in university of Calgary (Canada)

          The prerequisite for admission to graduate studies at University of Calgary is a bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college. A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is also required; however, admission will be granted without regard to GPA if an applicant has completed an honours program with distinction and/or has demonstrated exceptional academic achievement in their field.

            Ryerson University (Canada)

            Ryerson offers a four-year undergraduate program that can be completed entirely on-campus. However, most students choose to study abroad through Ryerson’s global exchange program; its partners include some prestigious universities such as University College London (UCL), Hanyang University (South Korea) and Imperial College London (UK). The duration of each exchange program varies—students can typically spend a semester or two at their overseas partner university.

              Eligibility for admission in Ryerson university

              The eligibility criteria differ from program to program. Some programs require a minimum admission average (GPA) while others rely on marks obtained at individual subjects. In addition to these entry requirements, you will also need to meet Ryerson’s English language requirements (minimum TOEFL score 600 or IELTS 5.5 band).

                York University (Canada)

                York University is a public research university in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. It is Canada’s third-largest university. York’s main campus is located in North York, an urban centre and one of five municipalities within the City of Toronto. The university has two satellite campuses: Keele Campus near Newcastle upon Tyne, England; and Glendon College at Glendon College (in Toronto). The campuses are approximately 150 kilometres (93 mi) apart.

                  Eligibility for admission in York university (Canada)

                  The student should have attained minimum 60% aggregate marks in 10+2/Intermediate. In case he/she has not completed 10+2/Intermediate then he/she must have passed class XII from a recognized Board with minimum 45% aggregate marks and an eligible candidate needs to be well conversant with English language. The applicants who are appearing at final year examination can also apply but they will not be considered till their results are declared.

                    Université de Montréal (Canada)

                    The Université de Montréal (UdeM) is a public research university in Montreal, Québec. It was established on 1 July 1965 following the merger of Laval University and Université de Montréal. Its campus is located on 132 hectares in Montréal’s Quartier Latin (Latin Quarter), adjacent to Montreal’s historic cultural neighbourhood.

                      Dalhousie University (Canada)

                      Dalhousie University (Dal) is a public research university located in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada. Dalhousie offers more than 4,000 courses and 180 degree programs in twelve undergraduate, graduate and professional faculties. In April 2016, 834 bachelor’s degrees were awarded. The annual tuition for international students at Dalhousie is CA$23,836; however please note that cost of living will vary depending on your lifestyle choices.

                        Eligibility for admission in Dalhousie university (Canada)

                        An applicant must complete their 10+2 or equivalent from a recognized board with marks at minimum 50% aggregate (45% in case of candidates belonging to reserved category). No particular subjects are mandatory for applying for any particular program. But application form will be rejected if any subject combination is entered which exceeds 20 credits.

                        Conclusion

                        For Indian students seeking education abroad, obtaining a student visa for Canada has always been quite easy. Each year a large number of students from India apply and get admissions to study at one of top law courses in Canada. No doubt that Canadian universities are among some of most reputed and oldest universities in North America with campuses spread across 8 cities from Vancouver to Halifax. The University admission process is generally straightforward but like any other foreign country they have their own rules and regulations that you need to follow while applying.
